title: Native code onboarder architecture: dedicated code index layer plus git diff incremental sync evidence chunk 1
summary: Design for the first-party AST repo onboarder and its two architecture questions, grounded in the existing graph (Explore map). LOCATOR-NODE LAYER (answer: separate layer, yes): the graph ALREADY has a derived layer — overlay.knowledge_nodes (source_doc/section/chunk/cluster) is a distinct map from authored note_nodes (lib/overlay.js:63-72,246-269), already excluded from the dup-judge (lib/judge.js iterates note_nodes only), the dashboard/delta (lib/delta.js:59-62), and the note-learner. BUT knowledge_nodes today are structural-expansion-only (surfaced via note->chunk traversal at base score 0.001, tier graph_expanded; lib/search/memory-search.js:313-387), NOT directly RAG-searchable — whereas the benchmark win (subconscious@cmm-KB full 0.583, beating cmm 0.551) came from DIRECT semantic retrieval of code-symbol notes. So code-locators must be a NEW dedicated code-index layer: a node kind `code_node` in its own overlay map (like knowledge_nodes: excluded from dup-judge/dashboard/learner/spec), BUT wired into /search RAG directly at its own tier+tunable weight so it is directly semantically searchable.
